problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={y}^{2}(t)-x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of differential equations above. What is the corresponding linearized system at the equilibrium point ${x}^{∗}=[0,\text{ }0]^{T}?$

| ${u}^{′}=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  | $\,\,u,\,$ where $u=x-{x}^{∗}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |  |  |
worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
{x}^{′}=f(x)
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and $f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-x \\ {x}^{2}+2y\end{aligned}].$

We need to compute the Jacobian matrix (or the total derivative) of $f(x).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}-x)=-1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}-x)=2y \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+2y)=2x,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+2y)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2y \\ 2x & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
{f}^{′}({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2(0) \\ 2(0) & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, near the equilibrium, the nonlinear system is approximated by

$$
{u}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]u,
$$

where the deviation vector is

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$
